plan.question: Can import-csv and the typed bundle readers establish the daily-session contract that mining horizons and evaluation annualization assume?
plan.expected: Trace a synthetic weekly series versus a daily history with missing sessions, explicit non-1d metadata, and the standard consumers. Classify pre-existing reports and concrete scope. Read one deterministic relevant unread ingress test slice.
plan.stop: Pin producer, typed reader and two consumer paths plus controls and independent disposition. No runtime claim on those traces.

proof.name: Producer
proof.expected: An XNYS session label represents a valid regular trading session. Publication as daily requires a truthful source interval declaration.
proof.observed: ISO complete dates are parsed and normalized, calendar is copied and frequency hardcoded to 1d. There is no source aggregation or supported-calendar validation in this path.

proof.name: Typed data boundary
proof.expected: Daily market_bars must have supported frequency and the consumer must reject contradictory labels before output.
proof.observed: Typed writer and reader require the fields and check adjustment and numeric invariants. Missing frequency is refused; a present explicit 1wk is not refused by those checks. Canonical content hash covers rows and schema.

proof.name: Mining
proof.expected: horizon_days is a count of trading sessions with causal entry after the decision.
proof.observed: Shared adjusted read enters observed-date panels and uses shifts by observed row index. Missing complete market dates and weekly bars can give longer economic periods than the label.

proof.name: Evaluation and benchmark
proof.expected: Valuation, delays, financing and annualization use the intended session axis. Daily benchmark gaps must not be bridged.
proof.observed: Run with no external benchmark and quantiles share the adjusted reader without a frequency gate. The external benchmark path rejects matching explicit non-1d metadata but only aligns to dates represented in market rows. The toy close-100/110/121 control traverses both retained closes after the middle market date is removed.

controls.input: Complete synthetic declared daily market, with enough dates and names and as-traded closes or disabled minimum price. Add a separate missing single-instrument session retaining another instrument's bar.
controls.expected: Supported daily workflows proceed, a per-name gap remains missing, and no data are filled to make an instrument tradable.

controls.case: Explicit unsupported interval and malformed typed metadata
controls.input: A validly shaped synthetic `market_bars` bundle declared 1wk. Add a malformed present-null frequency as a related control. Use a separately constructed fixture when a corrected typed publisher appropriately refuses to write the control.
controls.expected: Clear typed-boundary or option-specific refusal before ledger/result mutation in evaluate, search, confirm, default run or quantiles. Matching explicit weekly benchmark refusal stays covered, with affected existing test updated if the refusal moves to the source schema.

controls.case: Calendar membership and aggregation are distinct
controls.input: Valid XNYS session, ISO-valid XNYS Saturday and announced 2024-01-15 holiday, impossible ISO date, and legitimate non-XNYS synthetic weekday. Pair two identical OHLCV sparse-date grids whose independently declared source intervals differ.
controls.expected: A supported exchange calendar distinguishes valid and invalid sessions while preserving other supported calendars. Provenance distinguishes aggregation only when it specifies interval. Timestamp spacing alone cannot classify the pair.

controls.case: Whole-market gap vs single-instrument benchmark gap
controls.input: Synthetic market dates 2024-01-05 and 09 with a guaranteed middle session on Jan 08. Benchmark closes 100/110/121 across all three dates. Compare a dense market axis with only benchmark close Jan 08 missing.
controls.expected: No 21% two-session benchmark return is represented as a one-session daily observation. Preserve the existing per-benchmark-gap behavior. If publication allows intentionally sparse whole-market histories, make the rule for full-axis gaps explicit.

controls.input: Matching native Git for Windows Bash and native Python on current source with a synthetic snapshot and temporary ledger.
controls.expected: Retain pending successful ledger LF/CRLF and direct date-byte captures, valid replay, and invalid benchmark refusal without ledger mutation.
